Plot facet locations with qualified normal uncertainty bands

Source: R/api-plotting-extras.R
plot_rater_severity_profile.Rd

Ranks the levels of a chosen facet by fitted location and draws available normal uncertainty bounds around each point estimate. Optional descriptive bands mark absolute distances of 0.5 and 1.0 logit from zero; they are display aids, not calibration rules.

Usage 

plot_rater_severity_profile(
  fit,
  diagnostics = NULL,
  facet = "Rater",
  ci_level = 0.95,
  show_bands = FALSE,
  preset = c("standard", "publication", "compact", "monochrome"),
  draw = TRUE
)

Arguments

fit

An mfrm_fit from fit_mfrm().

diagnostics

Optional diagnose_mfrm() output. When omitted, diagnose_mfrm(fit, residual_pca = "none") is run internally. Supplied diagnostics must match the fitted analysis and current precision contract; they are reused without covariance recomputation.

facet

Facet name to plot (default "Rater"). Any non-Person facet name is accepted.

ci_level

Confidence level used for the whiskers (default 0.95). Bounds use +/- z * ModelSE (or SE only when the ModelSE column is absent). A missing ModelSE is not replaced rowwise.

show_bands

Logical, default FALSE. Explicit TRUE draws neutral gray +/-0.5 and +/-1.0 logit guides and describes them in the returned annotations. These distances are not equivalence bounds.

preset

Visual preset.

draw

If TRUE, draw with base graphics.

Value

An mfrm_plot_data object. Its data$data table contains columns Level, Estimate, SE, CI_Lower, CI_Upper, and Band, where Band contains numerical absolute-location ranges, not judgments about severity or quality. The ranges remain in the table when hidden. Other columns include Fixed, IntervalStatus, SEColumn, SE_Method, PrecisionTier, CIUse, CIEligible, SupportsFormalInference and the normal interval method/level. Source precision labels are retained; missing precision metadata cannot qualify an interval for inference. The enclosing data list retains the facet, confidence level and plot annotations and diagnostics identity check (source_status); keep these with the table when reporting the results. Fit readiness and interpretation notes are returned. Titles and notes are not automatically drawn.

Interpreting output

Zero is the sum-to-zero reference for the default centered facet; describe any different constraints or anchors used in the fit. With the default negative facet orientation, higher estimates reduce expected coded scores. This means stricter scoring when higher scores represent better performance; check the rubric direction before using that substantive interpretation. The axis names the selected facet's location rather than assuming that lower coded scores are less favorable. Returned notes state its fitted sign. The optional guides and numerical Band ranges describe distance from zero, not the sign of severity, operational interchangeability, or a need for training. No guide bands are drawn by default. Pairwise claims require the uncertainty of the contrast; check the SE basis in the supplied diagnostics. Two locations at -0.5 and +0.5 are one logit apart despite lying in the same range. A changed origin can change these ranges without changing pairwise differences. Use analyze_facet_equivalence() with a justified practical bound for equivalence; a non-significant difference does not establish it.

Here "profile" means an ordered display of facet locations, not a likelihood-profile confidence interval. Ordinary JML bands remain exploratory; MML fallback, regularized or review-only bands retain their restrictions. Plotting does not validate normal-approximation coverage. Fixed values use diamonds without sampling intervals. Crosses show finite points with unavailable or nonpositive SEs; unavailable estimates retain labeled rows. The horizontal range includes finite points even without SEs. as_ggplot() preserves these states, saved endpoints, guide bands and notes without fitting a model or recomputing an interval. Older saved plot payloads can reproduce their stored geometry but cannot acquire missing source or uncertainty qualifications through conversion. Older saved plots retain their original colored guides and Band labels (gentle, moderate, strict). Those labels never established equivalence. Regenerate the plot from the saved fit and matching diagnostics to obtain the neutral display; this does not require a new fit.

Migration in 0.2.4

This renderer is internal. Use the corresponding plot() route in mfrmr_plot_migration; the former exported name is no longer available.

Session plot defaults

Set options(mfrmr.plot_preset = "publication") to choose a session default for plotting functions that expose the common preset argument. The supported values are "standard", "publication", "compact" and "monochrome". Precedence is an explicit call argument, then the session option, then "standard". For example, preset = "standard" overrides a session set to "monochrome". Explicit preset = NULL retains the earlier package-default behavior; it does not read the session option. Invalid session values cause an error only when that option is needed.

The category-curve, data-quality, fit-review, connectivity and network routes of plot() for report bundles use the same option through .... Plots without a common preset argument, including extended-model plots with their own palette controls, keep their own settings. This option selects a preset, not a universal theme or a guarantee that all renderers implement every appearance control identically.

New plot payloads retain the resolved preset for supported saved-data rendering. Converting an existing payload with as_ggplot() uses its saved appearance, even after the session option changes. A call that creates a new plot from a fit or statistical result uses the current default. For a reproducible script, supply preset explicitly or set the option in that script. Saving only the fitted model does not save a session option. No global ggplot theme is changed.

Restore previous settings with old <- options(mfrmr.plot_preset = "monochrome") followed by options(old). Use options(mfrmr.plot_preset = NULL) to remove the option. The preset changes appearance, not estimates, confidence levels or diagnostic thresholds.

See also

diagnose_mfrm(), analyze_facet_equivalence(), plot(x, type = "facet_equivalence").

Examples 

library(mfrmr)

# Saved synthetic MML/RSM analysis of example_operational.
# For your own data, fit a model first; see ?fit_mfrm.
example_fit <- readRDS(system.file("examples", "operational-mml.rds", package = "mfrmr"))
fit <- example_fit$fit

# Use the diagnostics saved with this fit
diagnostics <- example_fit$diagnostics

# Compare signed severity estimates and their intervals
severity <- plot(fit, type = "rater_severity", diagnostics = diagnostics, show_bands = FALSE)

severity$data$data[, c("Level", "Estimate", "SE", "CI_Lower", "CI_Upper")]
#>    Level   Estimate        SE    CI_Lower    CI_Upper
#> 49   R01 -0.6059776 0.2243521 -1.04569977 -0.16625550
#> 50   R02 -0.3820356 0.2085513 -0.79078871  0.02671748
#> 52   R04  0.1799462 0.2226570 -0.25645356  0.61634590
#> 53   R05  0.1842365 0.2341852 -0.27475809  0.64323116
#> 51   R03  0.2120388 0.2165999 -0.21248930  0.63656689
#> 54   R06  0.4117917 0.2494894 -0.07719839  0.90078189
# Higher estimates mean stricter ratings with this example's default orientation
# The optional magnitude bands are omitted from this first comparison
